articleTitle: Popularity Block Labelling for Steiner Systems
abstract: Ordering the blocks of a design, the point sum of an element is the sum of the indices of blocks containing that element. Block labelling for popularity asks for the point sums to be as equal as possible. For Steiner systems of order v strength t in general, the average point sum is O(v<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2t-1</sup>); under various restrictions on block partitions of the Steiner system, the difference between the largest and smallest point sums is shown to be O(v<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(t+1)/2</sup> log v).

articleTitle: How to apply the rubber method for channels with feedback
abstract: We give an overview of applications of the rubber method. The rubber method is a coding algorithm that was developed in 2005 by Ahlswede, Deppe and Lebedev for channels with feedback. It was a big surprise that an encoding strategy which reserves one symbol exclusively as a rubber can sometimes reach the capacity of a channel. Since then, generalizations of the algorithm have been developed. These generalizations can be used for special channels. We also give other examples of modifications to the rubber method that achieve better results for certain channels.

articleTitle: A Class of Weak Keys for the QC-MDPC Cryptosystem
abstract: The quasi-cyclic moderate-density parity-check code (QC-MDPC) cryptosystem is one of the recent variants of the original McEliece code-based cryptosystem, that has also been part of the BIKE cryptosystem, which has been submitted to NIST as a post-Quantum cryptosystem candidate. We show that in certain cases the secret key can be recovered from the public key by means of a polynomial factorization. This leads to the concept of "weak keys" for the cryptosystem. Even though the probability of choosing a weak key at random is low, we are able to find weak keys quite easily. This suggests that avoiding weak keys may be introduced as a condition in the implementation of the cryptosystem.

articleTitle: Some parallelisms of PG(3, 5) involving a definite type of spread
abstract: There are 372 parallelisms of PG(3,5) which have been explicitly constructed and studied before the present paper. They contain all but one of the 21 nonisomorphic spreads of this projective space. It was not known by now if that particular spread can be included in a parallelism. We give a positive answer to this question by constructing parallelisms invariant under a cyclic group of order 8 some of which contain the spread. Useful invariants are calculated for all the obtained 899 new parallelisms of PG(3,5).

articleTitle: On interleaved rank metric codes
abstract: Horizontal and vertical interleavings of arbitrary matrix or vector rank metric codes are considered. A necessary and sufficient condition for an interleaved code to be maximum rank distance (MRO) code is obtained. In particular, horizontal interleaving of Gabidulin vector codes over the field F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</sub>m gives an example of a non-Gabidulin MRD code of length more than m. It is shown that interleaving of Gabidulin codes with different sets of locators can be decoded directly by syndrome decoders. Any other decoder can also be used in the case of different locators after making proposed modification of the received word.

articleTitle: A Parallel Algorithm for Computing the Weight Spectrum of Binary Linear Codes
abstract: We present a parallel SIMD (Single Instruction Multiple Data) algorithm for computing the weight spectrum of binary linear [n,k] codes using GPU (Graphics Processing Units) and CUDA (Compute Unified Device Architecture) programming platform. This algorithm is based on characteristic vector and Walsh-Hadamard transform and does not depend on the length of the code. We compare it with standard consecutive algorithms and give some experimental results.

articleTitle: On two-weight (linear and nonlinear) codes
abstract: We consider q-ary (linear and nonlinear) block codes with exactly two distances: d and d+δ. We obtain, as a necessary condition, a quadratic equation which relates the length n of the code to the remaining parameters. We also obtain upper bounds for the maximum size of such codes by utilizing a useful relation with two-distance spherical codes. Three tables of lower and upper bounds for alphabet sizes q =2, 3 and 4, respectively, are presented as examples.

articleTitle: Codes related to caps and the non-existence of some Griesmer codes
abstract: In this paper we consider the problem of class with parameters (q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> + 2q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> + q + 2, q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> + 2q + 2) in PG(3, q). Such arcs correspond to Griesmer [q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> + 2q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> + q + 2, 4, q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> + q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2-</sup>q]<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</sub>-codes. They are trivially obtained as the sum of a maximal cap in PG(3, q) and the whole geometry. We prove that for q = 5, 7 this is the only possible construction. This was known to be the case also for q = 4. For q = 3, there exists one further example. The characterization uses a divisibility result for plane blocking sets with parameters (q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, q-1) which is of independent interest.

articleTitle: On Covering Radius of Orthogonal Arrays
abstract: We obtain analytically upper bounds for the covering radius of orthogonal arrays (OAs) by investigations of the set of all feasible distance distributions of the corresponding OAs. We apply a procedure for reduction of the possible distance distributions of OA to improve the bound by 1 under certain assumptions. Examples of OAs attaining and close to our bounds are shown.

articleTitle: Binary LCD Codes Having an Automorphism of Odd Prime Order
abstract: The structure of binary LCD codes invariant under a permutation of odd prime order p is described. A systematic construction of such codes when 2 is a multiplicative root modulo p is presented. As an example, binary linear codes with complementary dual (or LCD codes) whose automorphism groups have orders divisible by 5 are constructed.

articleTitle: A Conjecture on Optimal Ternary Linear Codes
abstract: We give a conjecture on the achievement of the Griesmer bound for ternary linear codes. We prove that our conjecture is valid for at most 7 dimensions.

articleTitle: Systematic encoding for Z2s-linear codes
abstract: The ℤ(2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sup>)-additive codes are subgroups of ℤ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>(2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sup>). These codes can be seen as a generalization of linear codes over ℤ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and ℤ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>. A ℤ(2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sup>)-linear code is a binary code, not necessarily linear, which is the Gray map image of a ℤ(2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sup>)-additive code. In 2014, a systematic encoding was found for ℤ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>-linear codes. Moreover, an alternative permutation decoding method, which is suitable for any binary code (not necessarily linear) with a systematic encoding, was established. In this paper, we generalise these results by presenting a systematic encoding for ℤ(2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sup>)-linear codes with s > 2. This encoding allows us to perform a permutation decoding for this family of codes.

articleTitle: On the Formally Self-Dual Binary [30, 15, 8] Codes
abstract: We classify all binary linear [30, 15, 8] codes with dual distance 8 using the software package QextNewEdition. There are exactly 42 such codes and all of them are formally self-dual even codes. This result closes the long standing open problem about the existence of a formally self-dual odd code with these parameters.

articleTitle: Riemann-Roch Theorem and Mac Williams identities for an additive code with respect to a saturated lattice
abstract: Let (G, +) be a finite abelian group and (C, +)<; (G<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>, +) be an additive code with dual (C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⊥</sup>,.) <; (G<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>, + .). Consider a lattice (L, ∩, +) of subgroups of (G<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>, +) and its dual lattice (L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⊥</sup>, ., ∩) of subgroups of the character variety (G<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>, .). We say that L and L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⊥</sup> are saturated if their unique elements of maximal order are G<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> ∈ L, respectively, G<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⊥</sup> ∈ L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⊥</sup>. The present note generalizes Randriambololona's Riemann-Roch Theorem for sections of F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</sub>-linear codes C ⊂ F<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup><sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</sub> with values in subspaces of F<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup><sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</sub> to L-valued sections of C and L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⊥</sup>-valued sections of C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⊥</sup>. That provides natural Mac Williams identities for C, C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⊥</sup> with respect to saturated L, L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⊥</sup>. If C ⊂ F<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup><sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</sub> is an F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</sub>-linear code and (H, ∩, +) is the Hamming lattice of the coordinate subspaces of F<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup><sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</sub>, our Mac Williams identities reduce to the classical ones.

Author Keywords: Riemann-Roch Theorem for an additive code (C,+) < (Gn,+)
sections of C with values in a saturated lattice (ℒ,∩,+) of subgroups of (Gn,+)
Sobolev inner product of the support distribution function of C with respect to ℒ and a multiplicity function of ℒ
Mac Williams identities and Duursma’s function DLC(t) of C with respect to ℒ

articleTitle: Point-Counting on Elliptic Curves Belonging to One Prominent Family: Revisited
abstract: An approach to computing orders of elliptic curves from the family {D<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</sub> : y<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> = x<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> + ax (mod p), a ≠ 0} with p being a prime number, is presented. The method combines an explicit formula for the orders of curves reduced modulo p with the well-known Hasse bound. Besides its efficiency (the algorithm takes at most O(log<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> p) bit operations), this approach allows to determine in a transparent way the spectrum of curve orders when p is fixed.

articleTitle: Research Incentivization based on Smart Contract Platform
abstract: The boom of public blockchains and smart contract platforms opened new approaches to solve existing issues. These new approaches addressed successfully some weaknesses of previous processes and created some new classes of problems that need solutions. In this paper we explore distributed system based on smart contract platform with a low-entry barrier designed for direct incentivization of results of scientific research. The proposed system relies on transparent interactions between organizations and individual scientist defining hard computational problems with others that are willing to invest time and efforts searching for computational solutions.

articleTitle: Modern Software Lifecycle Management leveraging the power of Blockchain
abstract: Many distributed ledger technologies (DLT) offer smart contract platforms, that are already used in various industries such as healthcare, transportation, government, banking, and insurance. Software Lifecycle Management (SLM) is another area where DLT and smart contract platforms could play an important role in the future. SLM processes are covering the initial setup, technical and business configuration and ongoing maintenance of software systems that often consist of many cloud services, on-premise servers, and/or edge devices, spread on many geographical locations. In SLM there are many participants that should communicate each other to achieve common goal, for example the software provisioning. In case something wrong happens in their communication, it is very hard to prove what is the reason and which party failed to deliver, since the environment is complex and the protocols of responsibilities are not bound to the software dependencies. The purpose of this paper is to demonstrate how DLT-based smart contract platforms supports SLM processes for complex business systems where various participants are involved.

articleTitle: New lower and upper bounds on Armstrong codes
abstract: An Armstrong(q, k, n) code is a q-ary code of length n of minimum distance n - k +1 such that for every (k -1)-subset of coordinates there exists a pair of codewords that agree exactly there. Let f(q, k) denote the largest n such that an Armstrong(q, k, n) code exists. Upper and lower bounds on f(q, k) were given earlier in general, and in the case when k > k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>(q). In the present paper we propose a new construction to provide Armstrong((p+1)/2,2ℓ, p) for a prime p and give an upper bound in the case of fixed k and large enough q. Both results imply improvements on corresponding general known bounds for large enough q.

articleTitle: On the self-dual codes invariant under an automorphism of type 11-(8,0)
abstract: We study self-dual codes (SD) over GF(2) with 8 cycles of length 11 in the decomposition of its automorphism and minimum weight at least 16. The main method we use is by Huffman and Yorgov and is for constructing SD codes having an automorphism of order p for a prime p > 2. We prove that [8],[4] SD codes over F210 such that their preimage is a binary code with minimum weight 20 does not exist. By restricting the matrices of the subcode to have symmetric or circulant submatrix in their systematic form, we have found many new Hermitian self-dual codes over F210. Those newly found Hermitian codes allow us to constructed 468062 new binary SD [88,44,16] doubly-even codes.

articleTitle: On Identity-Based-Like Non-Interactive Key Establishment for Key Predistribution Schemes
abstract: We consider a problem of making key predistribution schemes more practical through computing pairwise keys non-interactively. For set intersection schemes this problem is reduced to computing a column of the incidence matrix of the scheme in identity-based manner. This will either reduce nodes' storage or communication overhead. We give simple yet computationally efficient procedures for two schemes: the Double-Complement (DC) construction and BAffine.For the 1- and 2-secure schemes based on the DC-construction any column of the incidence matrix can be computed in $O\left( {\log _2^2N} \right)$ operations on O(log<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> N)-bit numbers for a network of N nodes.For BAffine scheme, which is a composition of the affine plane of prime order q and Blom's scheme, we explicitly present the incidence matrix of the plane, and show that the number of the block of the plane common to any two points can be computed in 6 operations modulo q.Also we prove that the conjecture that the DC-construction could be scaled to a w-secure scheme for an arbitrary w is false. In particular, we show that for any w ≥ 3 and any matrices used in the DC-construction the resulting scheme is insecure.

articleTitle: Optimal Linear Codes Over the Field of Order 7
abstract: We construct some new linear codes over the field of order 7 to determine the exact value of the minimum length for which a linear code of dimension four with given minimum weight exists for some open cases. Most of the new codes are constructed as projective duals of some 7-divisible codes from some orbits of a projectivity in the projective space.

articleTitle: Investigation of the dependence of the evaluation parameters in protection of cardio data on the applied wavelet basis
abstract: The report presents an analysis of an algorithm for the protection of electrocardiological holter records of patients, including compression, watermarking and encrypting. Parameters were studied and analyzed using the latest technologies for analysis, processing and protection of digital information. Methods and technological approaches for organizing unstructured data with physiological information in digital repositories have been developed.The analysis is performed from the point of view of the choice of wavelet basis when performing wavelet transformation on the studied data and the influence of the specific selected basis on the next stages of the protection algorithm. An analysis of the protection procedure was performed using the Wavelet bases of Haar and Daubechies (Db) with 2, 4, 6, 8, 12 and 20 coefficients and 8 level of decomposition. The evaluation of the procedure was performed with the parameters PRD(Percentage Residual Difference) and PSNR (Peak Signal to Noise Ratio). The obtained results (PRD = 0.1724 and PSNR = 52.06 with Db4 and PRD = 0.1744 and SNR = 51.99 with Db8 show that the Dd4 and Db8 are the most suitable wavelet bases for performing watermarked procedure. After performing the encryption procedure, the following values are calculated PRD = 0.1802 and PSNR = 47.22 when applying Db4 basis.

articleTitle: Quantum codes from skew constacyclic codes over Fpm + vFpm + v2Fpm
abstract: For an odd prime p and m ≥ 1, let R = F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub>m[v]/{v<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>} = v}. Here our aim is to construct new non-binary quantum codes from skew constacyclic codes over this non-chain ring ℛ. In order to achieve our goal, first we study the structural properties of skew constacyclic codes and their Euclidean duals over the ring ℛ. Then we determine a necessary and sufficient condition for these codes to contain their Euclidean duals. Finally, by applying CSS construction on these dual containing skew constacyclic codes and using Gray map, we obtain several new quantum codes.

articleTitle: New QC Codes over GF(11)
abstract: A linear code of length n, dimension k and minimum distance d over GF (q) is denoted by [n, k, d]<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</sub>. One of the main problem in linear coding theory is - for given length and dimension to construct codes with best possible minimum distances. In this talk we present 10 new QC codes.

articleTitle: Single orbit affine generators for extended BCH codes with designed distance three
abstract: We show that for any prime p, p ≠ 2, 3 and any m, m ≥ 3 the narrow-sense BCH codes over GF (p) of length p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup> - 1 with designed distance three are not spanned by theirs minimum nonzero weight codewords. We prove that the extensions of these codes are spanned by their codewords of weight five and the bases could be chosen in the affine orbits of explicit codewords.

articleTitle: Three new large (n, r) arcs in PG(2,31)
abstract: A set of n points in PG(2,q) some r of which are collinear, but every r+1 are not collinear, forms an (n, r) arc. By m<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>(2, q) the maximum size of a such arc is denoted. In this talk (n, r) arcs with parameters (699, 24), (769, 26), and (838, 28) in PG(2,31) will be presented. The constructed arcs improve the respective lower bounds on m<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>(2, 31) in [8]. As a consequence there exist three new three-dimensional linear codes over GF(31).

articleTitle: New Linear Codes as Quasi-Twisted Codes from Long Constacyclic Codes
abstract: One of the most important and challenging problems in coding theory is to determine the optimal values of the parameters of a linear code and to explicitly construct codes with optimal parameters, or as close to the optimal values as possible. The class of quasi-twisted (QT) codes has been very promising in this regard. Over the past few decades various search algorithms to construct QT codes with better parameters have been employed. Most of these algorithms (such as ASR [1]) start by joining constacyclic codes of smaller lengths to obtain QT codes of longer lengths. There has been an algorithm that works in the opposite way that constructs shorter QT codes from long constacyclic codes. We modified and generalized this algorithm and obtained new linear codes via its implementation. We also observe that the new algorithm is related to the ASR algorithm.

articleTitle: Search for a Moving Element
abstract: We consider the moving element search problem with the minimum total cardinality of tests. As a search space, we consider the set of integer points of a segment of length n. We prove that the total test cardinality of an asymptotically optimal adaptive strategy is n + 2√n. Also we give an optimal strategy for non-adaptive case with the minimal number of tests.

articleTitle: Bounds and Code Constructions for Partially Defect Memory Cells
abstract: This paper considers coding for so-called partially stuck memory cells. Such memory cells can only store partial information as some of their levels cannot be used due to, e.g., wear out. First, we present a new code construction for masking such partially stuck cells while additionally correcting errors. This construction (for cells with q > 2 levels) is achieved by generalizing an existing masking-only construction in [1] (based on binary codes) to correct errors as well. Compared to previous constructions in [2], our new construction achieves larger rates for many sets of parameters. Second, we derive a sphere-packing (any number of u partially stuck cells) and a Gilbert-Varshamov bound (u <; q partially stuck cells) for codes that can mask a certain number of partially stuck cells and correct errors additionally. A numerical comparison between the new bounds and our previous construction of PSMCs for the case u <; q in [2] shows that our construction lies above the Gilbert-Varshamov-like bound for several code parameters.

articleTitle: On Software Implementation of Gabidulin Decoders
abstract: This work compares the performance of software implementations of different Gabidulin decoders. The parameter sets used within the comparison stem from their applications in recently proposed cryptographic schemes. The complexity analysis of the decoders is recalled, counting the occurrence of each operation within the respective decoders. It is shown that knowing the number of operations may be misleading when comparing different algorithms as the run-time of the implementation depends on the instruction set of the device on which the algorithm is executed.

articleTitle: New upper bounds on the maximal size of an arc in a projective Hjelmslev plane
abstract: In this paper we present new upper bounds on the size of an arc in the projective Hjelslev planes PHG(2, R), where R is a chain ring of mutilicity index 2.
